samples.text: The Union of the Comoros reiterates its support for the resolution adopted by the Summit of the Future (resolution 79/1) on 22 September, during this session of the Assembly. We call for genuine international collaboration to establish guidelines that will lead to legal tools guaranteeing the development and equitable use of artificial intelligence, conducive to development, growth, productivity and knowledge throughout the world. Among other things, the resolution opens up promising prospects for addressing the specific problems of small island developing States. In that context, the fourth International Conference on Small Island Developing States, held in May in Antigua and Barbuda, also marked further progress in this universal realization.

Since our last meeting here in September 2025, the genocide in Palestine has continued. Hundreds of thousands of Palestinian civilians, women, children, and elderly have lost their lives, and entire populations stand on the brink of extermination. The international community will regain its credibility first by taking urgent action to silence the guns, to protect civilian lives, whether Israeli, Palestinian, Lebanese, or Syrian, and ultimately implementing United Nations resolutions, including the two-state solution with Israel and Palestine coexisting peacefully. This is a prerequisite for addressing climate change. The risks of artificial intelligence and the imperative of sustainable development. We will make the right to development a pillar of multilateralism by facilitating access to sustainable funding and reducing inequalities globally. Ladies and gentlemen, please allow me to quote the great African writer Chinua Achebe. who said the following, "When we gather in the village under the moonlight, it's not because of the moon. Each person can see the moon in his own backyard. We gather because it is good to do so. Let us continue in a spirit of teamwork and draw strength from solidarity. If we smile together, it is not because we have no problems, but because we are stronger than our problems." Ladies and gentlemen, for half a century, the Comorian state, still striving for full sovereignty within its internationally recognized borders, remains under what it considers an illegal French occupation, despite the many relevant resolutions of this Assembly. The Comorian side has always favored a peaceful settlement of this dispute and has always believed that dialogue is the only alternative. And we have engaged in such a dialogue with France for two decades in an effort to reach a peaceful solution of this dispute once described by former French President Francois Mitterrand as unpleasant, and we regret that this dialogue has not succeeded. On the contrary, France's unilateral actions, particularly in Africa, run counter to our expectations.
